title: test_multihop_latency_bounds.py: chosen poll wait is the latency sample; CATASTROPHIC cannot fire
description:
## Problem

SECURITY false-confidence in the B.5.4 / 8.19.4 latency-bound suite after the 9098.5/9098.6 poll-after-airtime rewrite.

`python/tests/sim/test_multihop_latency_bounds.py` `_poll_after_hop_airtime` chooses `poll_at = tx_start + airtime - 1` (or `+ extra_delay_us` for LatencyRule), advances to that instant, then treats `sim.current_time_us - tx_start` as the measured hop latency. Every successful sample is therefore **the harness wait**, not an independently observed delivery time. Tests then lock that identity:

- non-chaos hops: `assert elapsed == airtime - 1` before `samples.append(elapsed)`
- LatencyRule hops: `assert elapsed == airtime + CHAOS_ADDED_US` (50 ms)

`_assert_harness_oracles` then applies `HOP_LATENCY_BUDGET_US` (300 ms), `MAX_P99_LATENCY_US` (500 ms), and `CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US` (1 s) to those samples.

SF10/125 kHz/CR4-5 airtime for these payloads is ~247.8 ms (`python/src/lichen/timing/airtime.py` fallback: 5–9 byte `pkt-*` / `chaos-*` / `stress-*` all yield `n_payload = 10` → 247808 µs). So:

- `airtime - 1` ≈ 247807 µs, always ≤ 300/500/1000 ms
- chaos: `airtime + 50_000` ≈ 297808 µs, always ≤ `HOP_LATENCY_BUDGET_US + CHAOS_ADDED_US`

The upper-bound asserts cannot fail unless PHY airtime itself exceeds the budget. Congestion (concurrent, bursty, sustained) does not add delay in this radio model: collisions drop, capture survivors are still sampled at `airtime - 1`.

## Catastrophic delay is sampled as loss, not a bound violation

If `radio.py` held a candidate for 10 s, `get_rx_result` at `airtime - 1` returns None. Callers skip (`if result:` / `if not result: continue` / `break`). The 10 s value is never appended. `CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US` / `HOP_LATENCY_BUDGET_US` never see it. Total miss fails only `MIN_DELIVERIES_FOR_STATS` (a delivery-rate check). Loss and unbounded delay are indistinguishable.

Closed `project-LICHEN-worker6-9098.5` acceptance required: "A hypothetical 10s hop would fail HOP_LATENCY_BUDGET_US / CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US." The rewrite does not meet that. It only made the chosen wait non-zero.

## LatencyRule lower bound is also by construction

`test_latency_bounded_with_added_delay` never polls during the injected window. There is no assertion that `get_rx_result("relay")` is None at `end_time_us` / `airtime - 1` and only becomes Some at `end_time_us + CHAOS_ADDED_US`.

If `_stash_delayed_rx_candidates` re-injected immediately after TxEnd and the eligibility filter were a no-op, the test would still wait until `airtime + 50 ms`, receive, and pass `elapsed == airtime + CHAOS_ADDED_US` and `min(relay_samples) >= CHAOS_ADDED_US`. Those asserts prove the wait length, not that ChaosEngine delayed delivery.

## Variance / consistency / max vs p99 are tautological

`test_latency_consistent_across_hops` still forces every hop to `airtime - 1`, then asserts hop-1 vs hop-3 mean ratio ≤ 2 and global max/min ≤ 2. All samples are the same PHY constant; ratio is identically 1.0. `test_sustained_load_latency_bounded` `max <= 2 * p99` is the same identity. 9098.5 asked for distinct per-hop poll times; that is not done.

Docstring still claims "end-to-end delay remains bounded under congestion load". Samples are per-hop PHY airtime only; a 4-hop path at ~248 ms/hop is ~1 s E2E and would still look in-budget.

## Why this is security (false confidence), not style

Green B.5.4 results currently certify hop-latency SLAs, chaos-delay injection, and "no catastrophic spikes" under load. Replay windows, OSCORE/EDHOC timeouts, and TDMA slot sizing (spec/02a) care about elapsed time. Operators could size those from vacuous evidence: the suite cannot falsify unbounded delay, cannot distinguish delay from drop, and cannot show LatencyRule was the reason a packet was late.

## Not a duplicate of 9098.4 / .5 / .6 / .7

- 9098.4 / .5: samples were ~0 µs from TX-start polls. Now samples are ~airtime, but still the **chosen poll offset**, and a 10 s hop still does not fail the budget asserts.
- 9098.6: chaos tests passed with `count == 0` / LatencyRule never waited. Now they wait and require `MIN_DELIVERIES_FOR_STATS`; they still do not probe unavailability during the delay or record late delivery as high latency.
- 9098.7: CUT metrics were the only oracle. Harness elapsed is now recorded and cross-checked; the harness clock is the wait the test scheduled.

## Files

- `python/tests/sim/test_multihop_latency_bounds.py` (`_poll_after_hop_airtime`, `_assert_harness_oracles`, chaos delay test, consistency/stress tests)
- `python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py` (`_get_rx_result_internal` latency filter + stash; delivery time is poll time)
design: Probe twice per hop: (1) poll at airtime-1 / end_time (must be None under LatencyRule, Some otherwise) (2) if modeling delay, poll again at a later bound. Record latency only from an actual RX; treat None-after-budget as a bound failure, not a skip. Assert payload identity against the TX. Keep CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US as a real ceiling on observed elapsed, not only on the scheduled wait. Consistency test must use distinct per-hop delays or an independent processing-time source, not airtime-1 vs airtime-1.
acceptance_criteria: A radio.py hold of 10s on every candidate fails HOP_LATENCY_BUDGET_US or CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US (not only MIN_DELIVERIES). LatencyRule test fails if get_rx_result succeeds at airtime-1 / end_time before added_us. Bound asserts are not implied by assert elapsed == scheduled_wait. test_latency_consistent_across_hops can fail when hop-1 and hop-3 delays differ by more than 2x.
close_reason: Dedicated LatencyRule injection >1s makes CATASTROPHIC fire on observed elapsed. 10s hold fails bound not MIN_DELIVERIES. Consistency uses distinct per-hop delays; >2x ratio fails.
